# 0067: A priced first-party release is catalogued or excluded before the curator writes it

Status: accepted, 2026-10-08.
Extends [0052](0052-scope-is-a-boundary-not-a-roster.md) (scope is a boundary, not a roster) with a decision owed for every id the boundary admits.
Extends [0059](0059-the-model-catalogue-is-one-config-file-beside-the-prices.md) with an `excluded` table beside each harness's models.
Extends [0060](0060-an-unpriced-model-is-priced-live-into-the-cache.md), which checks the other direction: a catalogued model with no price.

## Context

The curator's watch-list is a boundary, so a new release is priced without an edit (ADR 0052).
The catalogue is a roster, so a new release is swept only once someone adds it (ADR 0059).
`make test` closes the gap in one direction only: a catalogued model with no price curates a snapshot (ADR 0060).

The other direction had no check.
Claude Haiku 5.5 was released on 2026-10-07, and the feed priced it the next day.
`make prices` would have bundled its row without a word, and the default matrix would never have swept it.
The priced rows the catalogue already left out (gated models, previous generations, undated aliases) were left out silently.
Nothing told a reader those omissions were decisions.

## Decision

**Each harness in `models.toml` may carry an `excluded` table.** Each entry maps a model id to the reason it is left out.
The reason is a required non-empty string, and an id cannot be both catalogued and excluded.

**A priced first-party model that is neither catalogued nor excluded is undecided.** `derive/catalogue.py`'s `undecided` names every such model.

**The curator stops on an undecided model before it writes anything.** It names each one with the feed's `source` link and says where to decide it.
It does not guess a line, a tier or a release date, because those are hand-curated facts (ADR 0057).

**The weekly curation workflow asks for the decision.** When it stops on an undecided model, it opens or refreshes one "Undecided model releases" issue naming each model, and the run stays red.
Nobody has to watch the feed or name the new model to start an update.

**`make test` holds the bundled records to the same rule, offline.** A test fails when any bundled price row is undecided.

## Consequences

A new release is decided on the day the feed first prices it.
The decision is reviewed in the same diff as its price row.
Every model the plugin prices but does not sweep now has a stated reason in the one config file.

A feed that adds a variant spelling of an existing model, such as a dated snapshot, stops curation until someone writes one line.
That is deliberate: a snapshot may be a new model behind a familiar name.

## Lens

A boundary that admits a new model on its own is only half the job.
Someone still has to decide whether the plugin sweeps it.
Ask for that decision on the day the feed first names the model, and refuse to go on without it.
